items.title: Wayne Bergeron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 29, 2020
items.q: I was lucky enough to have a conversation with Joe Wilder, who did a lot in New York.

ctx.x: So you have to know when to do that. But you can. Not all contractors like that. They want you to shut up, they want it pin-drop quiet, and it usually is like that because everybody’s taking it very seriously of course. But that’s a way you can piss a contractor — but the showing up at the last minute, which I watched some musicians get drummed out of the business kind of. Because they would show up ten minutes before downbeat, which seems like plenty of time. But I’m the first one there. When I go to one of my…

Did that translate into the number of dates you would accept in one day? I remember, I was lucky enough to have a conversation with Joe Wilder, who did a lot in New York. And he would comment, he didn’t name names, but that people would accept multiple dates in a day knowing they weren’t going to be able to get to the third one on time.

You used to be able to get away with that at one point in this town. I mean there was a time when there was a lot of work and there was a lot of very high demand players, players that were doing everything, doing all the pop recording and just doing several sessions a day. And they’d take a 10:00 that’s supposed to go to 1:00 and then there’d be a 1:30 date across town and they would take it in hopes that they were going to get out early. And sometimes they were. And many times they’d go, “Oh we’re always done…
